title: Parliament has an AgoraEU deal. What did culture get?
content:
The article was updated on 21 November 2026 to reflect the budget figures in António Costa’s negotiating box.

On 19 November, the European Parliament’s Culture and Education (CULT) and Civil Liberties, Justice and Home Affairs (LIBE) committees achieved a compromise on AgoraEU, the EU’s programme for culture, media and civil society for 2028-2034. The vote sets the basis for Parliament’s position in further negotiations with the Commission and Council — the committees voted to enter interinstitutional negotiations on the basis of the compromise text.

For culture, there is much to welcome. MEPs want to secure the Culture strand’s share of the budget, strengthen provisions on working conditions and simplify funding procedures. Artists facing forced displacement would have dedicated support. The biggest concern is international cooperation: the compromise would make it even harder to work with organisations from countries that do not participate in the programme.
